title: control-plane: emit standardized incident annotations for routing degraded mode + attribution
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Internal: Control plane now emits versioned incident annotations (routing degraded-mode enter/exit + routing policy fallback) to support incident taxonomy attribution and dashboards.
description:
Summary: This PR adds a small, versioned "incident annotation" event emitted by the control plane for key reliability state transitions (starting with routing degraded mode enter/exit and policy fallback activation). These annotations are intended to be joined with incident records (Slack/incident-bot) for category attribution and trend reporting (e.g., routing overload vs capacity vs control-plane regression) without requiring responders to infer the root cause from sparse logs.

Motivation / context: During recent incidents (incl. SUP-1842 escalations) we’ve had repeated confusion about whether the system was in an intentional degraded mode (routing policy fallback, shed load, disable streaming to protect core) vs an unintended failure. The taxonomy v1 work also needs consistent, machine-generated signals to reduce postmortem reclassification churn and to power dashboards by category/impacted surface.

What’s included: - New event type: control_plane.incident_annotation.v1 (JSON payload + protobuf mirror for internal bus) - Annotation kinds implemented in this PR:   - routing.degraded_mode.enter   - routing.degraded_mode.exit   - routing.policy_fallback.activated   - routing.policy_fallback.deactivated - Common fields:   - annotation_id (uuid)   - schema_version ("v1")   - emitted_at (RFC3339)   - env (prod/staging)   - region (e.g., us-east-1)   - deployment_surface (hosted|dedicated|private)   - customer_tier (unknown|self_serve|enterprise) (best-effort; remains unknown for some internal transitions)   - impacted_surface (routing|gateway|scheduler|fleet|runtime|control_plane) (controlled vocabulary; see below)   - category_hint (routing_degraded_mode|routing_policy_fallback) (hint only; incident-bot remains source of truth)   - severity_hint (none|sev3|sev2|sev1) (optional; currently set only for enter events)   - reason_code (small enum; avoids free-form strings)   - details (small map; heavily constrained to avoid high-cardinality)

Vocabulary alignment: impacted_surface + category_hint values are aligned with the incident metadata allowed-values list being rolled out in ENG-4822/ENG-4825. This PR does not attempt to define the full taxonomy; it emits signals that help attribution and time-correlation.

Data plumbing: - Emits to the existing telemetry event bus (kafka topic: telemetry.annotations) with a new dataset name "incident_annotations" - Adds OTEL span events on control-plane routing decision spans with a stable attribute set (so we can correlate in tracing when needed) - Adds a small rate limiter (token bucket) per (annotation_kind, region) to prevent spam on flapping transitions

Guardrails: - No customer content, prompts, or request payloads are included - details map is limited to a whitelist of keys (e.g., policy_name, degraded_mode_profile, router_pool) and values are length-limited - Cardinality controls: policy_name is normalized to a short ID; router_pool uses a controlled set

Rollout plan: - Behind flag: ControlPlane.EmitIncidentAnnotations (default OFF) - Staging: enable globally for 24h, validate dataset volume + schema in dashboards - Prod: enable for Hosted first (us-east-1 + eu-west-1), then Dedicated pools

Testing: - Unit tests for schema serialization + whitelist enforcement - Integration test: toggling degraded mode results in exactly one enter/exit annotation per transition (debounce window = 30s) - Load test in staging to validate rate-limiter behavior

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Add annotations for autoscaler safe-mode + fleet provisioning stalls (Infra requested) - Add cross-region routing failover enter/exit annotations - Wire dashboards (ENG-4827) to overlay annotation timelines on incident MTTR charts

Checklist: - [x] Schema reviewed with Observability - [x] Flagged + safe default - [x] Docs added to internal README for telemetry events - [x] Backwards compatible (new dataset only)
commits: control-plane: add incident annotation schema + serializer (v1)
telemetry: add incident_annotations dataset registration + topic routing
routing: emit policy fallback activate/deactivate annotations
otel: attach annotation events to routing decision spans
tests: add whitelist + cardinality guard tests
docs: describe incident annotation events + examples
review_conversation: Mina Haddad: Can we confirm the boundary between routing.degraded_mode vs routing.policy_fallback? In past incidents responders conflated them; want the annotation kinds to be mutually exclusive.

Ethan Park (author): Yep. degraded_mode is a global routing behavior change (shed load / change queuing strategy). policy_fallback is a specific policy evaluation path (fallback to compatible model/region). They can co-occur; kinds remain distinct. I added reason_code enums per kind and documented the difference in docs/internal/telemetry/incident-annotations.md.
Logan Wright: Concern about high-cardinality in details: policy_name and router_pool can explode if we aren’t careful. Are we normalizing these and do we have a hard whitelist?

Ethan Park (author): Added a strict whitelist (policy_id, degraded_mode_profile, router_pool_id) + length limits; policy_name is converted to policy_id (short stable ID from config). Added tests to reject non-whitelisted keys and long values.
Allison Grant: Please align impacted_surface values with the allowed set in the incident metadata standard. Also can we include schema_version as a top-level field for downstream mapping stability?

Ethan Park (author): Updated impacted_surface to controlled set (routing|gateway|scheduler|fleet|runtime|control_plane) and added schema_version="v1" to the top-level. Also added a note that category_hint is not authoritative.
Sean Gallagher: Operationally, I want to be sure this won’t create noise during flapping. What’s the debounce strategy? Also, do we page on these annotations?

Ethan Park (author): Debounce window is 30s and there’s a per-kind token bucket. This PR does not add paging; it only emits annotations. Paging decision will live with dashboard/alert work (ENG-4827) and SRE tuning.
Sergio Costa: For dashboards, I’d prefer emitted_at in RFC3339 UTC and a stable region field. Also: do we have a sample event in docs?
Ethan Park (author): emitted_at is UTC RFC3339; region is cloud region string. Added two sample payloads in the doc and ensured schema validation enforces required fields.
Allison Grant: Approved after the whitelist + schema_version changes. Thanks.
Sean Gallagher: Approved (flag default OFF + debounce/rate limit looks fine).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Ethan Park; feature flag remains OFF by default. Follow-up task tracked in ENG-4827 for dashboard wiring + validation in prod.
